method: Ideal horizontal centre-range only, one-unit midpoint bins; gun/Arc48/72, inactive gun96 and silo72/96/120. Separate production geometry/LOS/pitch/contact/flight reports govern selected designs. Each plot is an independent alternative; overlapping route intervals are not additive damage.

options.title: Cistern and Mesa Circuit
options.rationale: The west entry bends around a small early court, returns north beside the cistern aqueduct, crosses the central dry garden and circles the eastern mesa before a separate southern catch. The two raised mesa islands and small cistern remain intact scenery. North/central firing choices trade against a longer eastern exposure and a late southern return.

options.title: Southern Mesa Return
options.rationale: A west entry skirts the southwestern mesa, turns through a southern court and returns north between the two raised islands. An eastern ascent and long eastern descent lead to a southeast exit. The southern landform has a stronger role, while the cistern and northern aqueduct stay remote scenery and the eastern side receives a long uninterrupted exposure.

options.title: Riverfold Crossing
options.rationale: The western bank first curls through a dry lower court. One short straight crossing at the river waist introduces the eastern bank, whose northern court and eastern return lead around the raised aqueduct to an independent southern catch. The winding river remains a continuous dominant feature and the aqueduct fragments remain on their original raised ground.

options.title: Aqueduct Confluence
options.rationale: A longer western approach visits the lower bank and upper aqueduct before a two-box bridge; a shorter northeastern approach curls through its own dry court. They meet east of the river and share a late southeast return. This creates bank/branch investment choices, at the cost of a larger western scenic carve and uneven approach lengths.

options.title: Three Mesa Tour
options.rationale: One long journey returns north around the western mesa, passes the small northern pool and skirts the lower face of the eastern mesa. It then descends the east and circles the southern mesa before a southwestern catch. It engages the greatest depth of the landscape, with a substantial scenic cost and delayed repeated encounters.

options.title: Mesa Confluence
options.rationale: A western approach bends through a broad central court while an eastern approach wraps below the northeastern mesa and aqueduct. They meet east of the southern mesa, then circle it through a southern return and independent southwest catch. Western-only, eastern-only and shared investments stay spatially distinct without turning every junction into one compact dominant court.

options.title: Aqueduct and Shore Tour
options.rationale: A northern entrance runs down the dry eastern mainland, turns around the broken aqueduct, then returns along the indented eastern lake shore. A lower court and southeast turn supply a distinct final catch. The broad western lake remains uninterrupted; the raised northern and southeastern mesas remain landmarks rather than roads.

options.title: Basin Confluence
options.rationale: A northeastern approach descends the mainland while a southern approach climbs the lake shore, meeting beside the aqueduct before one shared lower court and southeast exit. This offers early branch-specific choices on constrained land, but concentrates more coverage around the common shore junction and uses less of the northern dry entry.
